title: Multi-Clause Functions & The Punctuation Triad (, ; .)
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates multi-clause function dispatch, the punctuation triad (; vs .), and repeated pattern variable matching.

otpDocCards.description: Exception raised when no clause pattern in a function matches the supplied arguments.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Standard runtime error reporting top-to-bottom clause exhaustion.

mentalModelCheck.question: In an Erlang multi-clause function, what happens if you end the first clause with a period (.) instead of a semicolon (;)?

options.label: The compiler terminates the function definition prematurely and throws a syntax error on the next clause
options.explanation: A period marks the full stop of the entire function. Semicolons must separate individual clauses.

options.label: The compiler treats the period as an automatic fallback return statement
options.explanation: Erlang has no return keyword or fallback punctuation; the period only terminates definitions.

options.label: The BEAM VM executes both clauses concurrently on separate schedulers
options.explanation: Punctuation controls sequential syntax compilation, not concurrent execution.
